title: うち: inside the boundary
summary: うち is an enclosure defined by its contents: home, our group, a span of time, and a pool to choose from.

blocks.text: **うち** is an enclosure, defined by what is inside it. Every meaning comes from that one picture.

rows: home (family life, not just the building)
the in-group vs. outsiders (うち / そと)

blocks.text: いえ is the building; **うち** is the family life inside it. Compare the two.

Japanese often says うちの to mean "our": うちの母, even with no big difference between self and group. This is the **うち / そと** (in-group / out-group) split that shapes language, including くれる, which gives **down to** our group (lesson 11).

blocks.jp: うちの犬はよく吠える。

blocks.text: In Kansai speech, and for girls in anime, うち can mean "I" itself. A noun + んち is a casual "someone's place", short for うち.

blocks.en: I'm heading home now. (Kansai-style うち = I)
Let's go to Sakura's place. (さくらんち = さくらのうち)

blocks.text: The enclosure can be a group, and うち then means "among". Use it to pick one or several out of the group.

blocks.jp: 三つのうち一つだけ選んでください。
blocks.en: Please choose just one of the three.

blocks.jp: 多くの本のうちから、これを選んだ。
blocks.en: I chose this one from among many books.

blocks.text: A noun or clause + うちに means "while it lasts": the time is an enclosure defined by its contents.

blocks.en: Please enjoy it while it's warm.

blocks.jp: 今のうちに勉強しよう。
blocks.en: Let's study while we still can.

blocks.text: With a negative, ないうちに means "before it happens". With a verb in the ている form, ているうちに means "while doing it, before I knew it".

blocks.jp: 暗くならないうちに帰ろう。
blocks.en: Let's go home before it gets dark.

blocks.jp: 歩いているうちに、道がわからなくなった。
blocks.en: While I was walking, I lost my way before I knew it.

blocks.text: 今のうち means "while the present situation lasts". そのうち is "in that enclosure", something vaguely coming in the near future.

items: うち = an enclosure defined by its contents.
**今のうち** = while we still can; **そのうち** = sooner or later.

questions.instruction: Which word means the family life inside a house?
questions.note: うち is the interior; いえ is the building.

questions.instruction: What does うちの母 emphasize?
questions.note: Group identity.

questions.instruction: What does 今のうち mean?
questions.note: While the present situation continues.

questions.instruction: What does そのうち mean?
questions.note: A vague future.

questions.prompt: いえ refers mainly to the physical building.
questions.note: うち is the family life inside.

questions.instruction: What does うち mean here?
questions.note: Some speakers use うち for "I".

questions.instruction: Which phrase picks one out of a group?
questions.note: のうち: among the group.

questions.prompt: 忙しくならない＿＿に、友達に会おう。
questions.note: Clause + うちに: while it lasts.
questions.en: Let's see our friends while we're not busy yet.

questions.prompt: 冷たい＿＿に飲んでください。
questions.note: 冷たいうちに: while it is still cold.
questions.en: Please drink it while it's cold.

questions.note: うちの: our family's.
questions.en: My father (our dad) is a teacher.

questions.note: そのうち: sooner or later.
questions.en: Let's meet again sooner or later.

questions.prompt: 若い＿＿に、いろいろな国へ行きたい。
questions.note: 若いうちに: while I'm young.
questions.en: I want to visit many countries while I'm young.

questions.instruction: What does 今のうちに mean here?
questions.prompt: 今のうちに宿題をしておこう。
questions.note: 今のうち: while the present situation lasts.
questions.en: Let's do the homework while we still can.

questions.instruction: Which sentence uses いえ for the building?
questions.note: 家 is the building; うち is the family life inside.

questions.instruction: What does うち mean here?
questions.prompt: この三つのうち、どれが好きですか。
questions.note: A group to choose from.
questions.en: Of these three, which do you like?

questions.note: Clause + うちに: while it lasts.
questions.en: Let's go home while it isn't raining.

questions.note: うちの: our (my group's).

questions.instruction: Tap the word that means "sooner or later"
questions.note: そのうち: some time soon.
questions.en: It'll stop raining sooner or later.

questions.prompt: Let's go while it's still early.
questions.note: い-adjective + うちに.
questions.en: Let's go while it's still early.

questions.prompt: Let's eat before it gets cold.
questions.note: Negative + うちに: before it happens.
questions.en: Let's eat before it gets cold.

questions.prompt: Before I knew it, I fell asleep while reading.
questions.note: ているうちに: while doing it, before I knew it.
questions.en: Before I knew it, I fell asleep while reading.

questions.prompt: Sooner or later you'll surely understand.
questions.note: そのうち: sooner or later.
questions.en: Sooner or later you'll surely understand.

questions.prompt: In 若いうちに, うち means the place called home.
questions.note: Here it is an enclosure of time: while I'm young.
んち is a casual short form of うち.
